operations.content: Personal financial dashboard built on a Finviz Elite subscription, for both real research/trading use and as a learning project. Local-only, single-user, no auth needed.

8-phase roadmap: 1) foundation + stock lookup, 2) screener, 3) options chain viewer (Schwab API), 4) watchlists + alerts, 5) options strategy suggestions, 6) insider/institutional feed, 7) news + sentiment, 8) portfolio tracking + backtesting. Order front-loads the two biggest unknowns (Finviz export API, Schwab API auth).

User is an experienced software engineer but new to financial/trading APIs. Wants domain-specific quirks (Finviz export semantics, options mechanics, market data behavior) documented in code/docs, but doesn't need general software engineering explained.
Backend: Python + FastAPI. Frontend: React + TypeScript (Vite). Chosen so pandas can handle Finviz's CSV-shaped export data and screener manipulation naturally.
SQLite for local persistence (response cache, later saved screens/watchlists/portfolio data). Chosen over Postgres since this is local-only single-user.
Docker Compose used for local dev (backend, frontend, SQLite volume as services), not plain local processes, per explicit user preference.
Finviz Elite export API (CSV endpoints at export.finviz.com, auth via static token in URL) for quotes/screener/fundamentals. Finviz has NO options data at all (no chains, IV, or greeks) on any tier.

Schwab developer API (user has a Schwab/thinkorswim brokerage account) will supply options chains and greeks. Requires a developer app approval process that can take days, so should be started early/in parallel.
Backend owns all external API calls (Finviz, Schwab); frontend never calls them directly. Keeps the Finviz Elite token and Schwab credentials server-side only, never shipped to the browser.

A finviz_client module wraps Finviz's CSV export endpoints and cryptic filter codes behind typed Python functions (get_quote(ticker), run_screener(filters)); rest of app never touches raw CSV/URL-encoding or Finviz filter codes directly.
Brainstorming/design phase complete for Phase 1 (foundation + stock lookup). Writing design spec doc next, then an implementation plan.

After phase 1 spec is approved: invoke writing-plans skill for the phase 1 implementation plan. Later phases (screener, options/Schwab, watchlists, etc.) each get their own brainstorm -> spec -> plan cycle.
